title: WALMART DEFERRED COMPENSATION MATCHING PLAN

nodes.title: WALMART DEFERRED COMPENSATION MATCHING PLAN (intro)
nodes.summary: The amended Walmart Deferred Compensation Matching Plan, effective February 1, 2023, covers its purpose, effective date, and nature; definitions; participant deferrals, deferred bonuses, employer matching credits, account allocations, and election rules; account crediting and valuation; benefit payments, including scheduled, separation, death, emergency, and tax-related distributions and misconduct reductions; plan administration and claims and appeals procedures; and miscellaneous provisions concerning amendment or termination, non-alienability, overpayments, employment and bonus rights, taxes, successors, and governing law.

nodes.title: ARTICLE I. GENERAL
key_items: 1.1 Purpose.; 1.2 Effective Date.; 1.3 Nature of Plan.
nodes.summary: The amended Walmart Deferred Compensation Matching Plan took effect February 1, 2023, to let eligible employees defer compensation, receive employer matching credits and earnings, and save beyond 401(k) limits. It is an unfunded, unsecured ERISA plan for select management/highly compensated employees, paid from Walmart’s general assets and administered under Code Section 409A. Definitions cover accounts and pre-/post-2021 classes, deferral and matching credits, compensation and bonuses, eligibility, employers and affiliates, plan administration and investment terms, misconduct, disability and emergencies, separation from service and payment dates, in-service and retirement accounts, participation years, and related tax and valuation rules.

summary: The amended Walmart Deferred Compensation Matching Plan, effective February 1, 2023, enables eligible select management and highly compensated employees to defer compensation and bonuses, receive employer matching credits and investment earnings, and save beyond 401(k) limits. The unfunded, unsecured ERISA plan is paid from Walmart’s general assets and administered under Code Section 409A. It defines participant and account categories, eligibility, compensation, credits, investments, valuation, disability, emergencies, separation and payment terms; establishes deferral elections, allocations, crediting, and scheduled, separation, death, emergency, and tax-related distributions, including misconduct reductions; and sets out administration, claims and appeals, amendments and termination, non-alienability, overpayments, employment and bonus rights, taxes, successors, and governing law.

title: ARTICLE III. DEFERRAL CREDITS AND MATCHING CONTRIBUTION CREDITS AND ACCOUNT ALLOCATIONS

nodes.title: 3.1 Deferred Compensation.
nodes.summary: Eligible Officers may defer all or part of annual compensation, capped at 80% for Plan Years beginning on or after February 1, 2022, while retaining enough pay for required taxes, insurance premiums, and other permitted withholdings. Deferrals are prorated across payroll periods; a period spanning Plan Years uses the election for the year in which it ends. Elections must use Plan Administrator-approved forms. Existing officers must elect by December 31; newly eligible officers generally have 30 days, subject to specified prior-plan eligibility or payment conditions. New-officer elections apply only to later payroll periods and must meet Code Section 409A requirements. Deferred amounts are credited to the officer’s Deferral Account and allocated to a Retirement or Scheduled In-Service Account under Section 3.5.

nodes.title: 3.2 Deferred MIP Bonuses.
nodes.summary: Eligible Participants may defer all or part of an MIP bonus for a performance period coinciding with or ending in a Plan Year; non-officers are limited to 80%. Elections cannot reduce pay below required taxes, insurance premiums, or other permitted withholdings and must use Administrator-approved forms. Elections are generally due before the performance period; qualifying 12-month performance-based bonuses may use a later deadline, and newly eligible officers may elect within 30 days subject to 409A eligibility rules. Such elections apply only to post-election services, with the deferrable bonus prorated by remaining performance-period days. Deferred bonuses are credited to the participant’s Plan Year Deferral Account and allocated to a Retirement or Scheduled In-Service Account under Section 3.5.

nodes.title: 3.3 Deferred Special Bonuses.
nodes.summary: Eligible Officers may defer all or part of a Special Bonus using an Administrator-approved form. Elections cannot reduce pay below required taxes, premiums, and other permitted withholdings; the election date is when the Administrator receives the executed form. Deferral is allowed only for qualifying bonuses: (1) service-conditioned bonuses requiring at least 13 months of continued service, with no earlier vesting for good-reason termination or retirement, meeting Code Section 409A requirements, elected within 30 days of obtaining a binding right; or (2) bonuses specified as deferrable in a written, pre-employment offer letter, elected before any services begin. Deferred amounts are credited to the officer’s Deferral Account and allocated to a Retirement or Scheduled In-Service Account under Section 3.5.

nodes.title: 3.4 Employer Matching Contribution Credits.
nodes.summary: Eligible participants employed by the Employer or a Related Affiliate at year-end, with no separation during the Plan Year, may receive a matching credit based on Deferred Compensation and Deferred MIP Bonus credited that year, capped at 6% of Excess Compensation. No match applies to deferrals withdrawn under Section 5.5; credits are allocated under Section 3.5. Matching accounts and earnings vest after three Years of Participation, or earlier upon death before separation or disability. Distribution under Article V requires vesting as of separation.

nodes.title: 3.5 Account Allocation Elections
nodes.summary: Participants must allocate each compensation, MIP bonus, or Special Bonus deferral to a Retirement or Scheduled In-Service Account, and allocate related employer matching credits to a Retirement Account. Their first Retirement Account allocation requires choosing a permitted distribution form; their first Scheduled In-Service Account allocation requires choosing a scheduled pay date. If no allocation is elected, the prior Plan Year’s allocation for the same category applies. If none exists, pre-February 1, 2021 amounts go to an applicable existing Retirement Account (or are divided equally among multiple accounts); absent one, a permitted Retirement Account with lump-sum payment is deemed elected. For amounts attributable to Plan Years beginning on or after that date, a lump-sum Retirement Account under the applicable Class Account is deemed elected.

nodes.title: 3.6 Irrevocability of Deferral Elections and Account Allocation Elections.
nodes.summary: Deferral and account-allocation elections generally cannot be changed after their applicable deadlines or election dates, and do not carry over to later Plan Years without a new election. Separation from Service ends Section 3.1 compensation elections after the last regular paycheck, with same-year rehire reinstating them; Sections 3.2–3.3 bonus elections remain applicable to the relevant bonus, including after rehire. Loss of Eligible Officer status ends compensation elections the following January 31, with proration if compensation falls; short-term disability-related reductions also require proration. Loss of Eligible Participant status ends Section 3.2 elections for performance periods beginning the next calendar year, while Section 3.3 elections remain in effect when an Eligible Officer loses that status. Unpaid leave pauses Section 3.1 elections, which resume upon same-year return; applicable compensation paid during leave and Sections 3.2–3.3 elections are unaffected.

nodes.title: 3.7 Automatic Suspension of Deferral Elections.
nodes.summary: If a Participant seeks a distribution or deferral cancellation due to an Unforeseeable Emergency, and the Plan Administrator or delegate determines that stopping deferrals may relieve it, some or all deferral elections under Sections 3.1–3.3 for that Plan Year, as determined by the administrator or delegate, must be cancelled as soon as administratively practicable.

summary: The section governs elections to defer compensation, MIP bonuses, and qualifying Special Bonuses, including eligibility, limits, deadlines, withholding protections, proration, 409A requirements, and account credits. It sets matching-credit eligibility, limits, allocation, and vesting; requires allocation of deferrals and matches to Retirement or Scheduled In-Service Accounts, with default allocations and payment choices; specifies when elections become irrevocable or end due to status changes, separation, disability, or leave; and requires suspension of deferrals when deemed necessary to address an Unforeseeable Emergency.

title: ARTICLE IV. ACCOUNTS AND TIMING OF CREDITS TO ACCOUNTS
key_items: 4.2 Deferral Credits and Employer Matching Contribution Credits.; 4.3 Valuation of Accounts.
4.2 Deferral Credits and Employer Matching Contribution Credits.
summary: Participant accounts are bookkeeping measures only, remain Walmart’s property, and provide an unsecured right to plan benefits. Deferrals and bonuses are credited after they otherwise would be paid; matching credits are posted at year-end, with timing depending on whether the Plan Year began before or on/after February 1, 2023. Accounts are maintained until benefits are fully paid and valued monthly. Pre-investment amounts earn either monthly compounded interest or deemed investment-option returns, subject to irrevocable elections during administrator-set windows; absent an election, interest applies. Post-investment amounts receive deemed investment-option returns. The administrator sets election procedures, but Walmart need not actually invest funds.

title: ARTICLE V. PAYMENT OF PLAN BENEFITS

nodes.title: 5.1 Scheduled In-Service Benefits.
nodes.summary: Scheduled in-service accounts are paid as a lump sum within 90 days after the applicable Scheduled Pay Date, based on the account’s value on that date. If, before that date, an event triggers an earlier distribution under Section 5.2 or 5.3, the account is instead distributed under the applicable section.

nodes.title: 5.2 Separation Benefits.
nodes.summary: Upon separation from service, Scheduled In-Service Accounts are paid as a lump sum, while Retirement Accounts follow the participant’s effective distribution election. Lump sums are paid within 90 days after the Separation Pay Date and valued as of the preceding month-end. Annual installments begin within 90 days after the first applicable January 31, or the Separation Pay Date if earlier, with later installments following each January 31. Interest-credited portions are amortized in equal annual payments using the specified interest rate; earnings-, gains-, and losses-credited portions are paid in substantially equal installments based on the remaining balance divided by installments remaining.

nodes.title: 5.3 Death Benefits.
nodes.summary: If a participant dies before separation or benefit commencement, the account is paid under the effective election; one payment form must apply to all beneficiary levels, and absent an effective election, payment is a lump sum. Lump sums are paid within 90 days after the month of death and valued as of the preceding month-end. Annual installments begin within 90 days of the first January 31 on or after death and recur annually; interest-credited portions use equal amortizing payments at the applicable rate, while investment-credited portions use substantially equal payments based on the remaining balance and installments. If death follows installment commencement, payments continue to the beneficiary in the same form, except an applicable lump-sum election requires the remainder to be paid within 90 days after the month of death. Participants may file and change beneficiary designations; absent surviving designees, payment follows the stated priority: spouse, children, parents, siblings, then estate. If a beneficiary dies before full payment, their share passes equally to remaining beneficiaries at that level, then the next level, or—if none—to that beneficiary’s spouse, children, parents, siblings, or estate, in priority order.

nodes.title: 5.4 Form of Distribution.
nodes.summary: Upon separation from service, or death before separation, participants may elect a lump sum, up to 15 years of substantially equal annual installments, or—only for death distributions—a combination, subject to $50,000 minimums. The threshold applies to the relevant Pre-2021 account or combined Post-2020 accounts; below it, payment defaults to a lump sum when the first installment otherwise would be due. Subsequent elections must follow administrator procedures and 409A timing limits: a 12-month effectiveness delay, generally a five-year payment delay, filing at least 12 months before payment, and completion by the Plan Year containing the 20th anniversary of separation pay date or death; death is excepted from the five-year delay, and installments count as one payment. Invalid elections are disregarded in favor of the latest valid election. Required elections and scheduled pay dates must be filed on administrator-approved forms.

nodes.title: 5.5 Distributions for Unforeseeable Emergencies.
nodes.summary: For an Unforeseeable Emergency, the Plan Administrator may, in its discretion and upon written application by the participant or eligible beneficiary, authorize an immediate distribution, excluding unvested matching-account amounts. The distribution is limited to the need and anticipated related taxes and penalties, after considering insurance, non-hardship asset liquidation, and stopping deferrals. It is drawn first from current-year scheduled in-service accounts, then current-year retirement accounts, then proportionately from remaining balances in those account types. For distributions before January 1, 2021, payment must be suspended to the extent a deduction would be barred under Code Section 162(m), until a deduction is reasonably expected to be allowed and the emergency conditions still apply.

nodes.title: 5.6 Distributions for Payment of Taxes.
nodes.summary: The Plan Administrator may accelerate a lump-sum payment from a Participant’s benefits to cover FICA taxes and related income-tax withholding, as well as applicable state, local, or foreign taxes and related withholding on deferred Plan amounts, before those amounts are paid or made available to the Participant.

nodes.title: 5.7 Reductions Arising from a Participant’s Gross Misconduct.
nodes.summary: Benefits are contingent on avoiding Gross Misconduct during employment with an Employer, Related Affiliate, or Walmart-owned entity, and any additional period under Walmart’s Statement of Ethics. If the Plan Administrator finds misconduct, the Participant forfeits matching contribution credits and related earnings; earnings on Deferral Accounts and any remaining installments are recalculated using 50% of the applicable rate, though net losses are not adjusted. Deferred Compensation, Deferred MIP Bonus, and Deferred Special Bonus cannot be forfeited. If misconduct is found after payment, the Participant or beneficiary must repay amounts exceeding entitlement. The text then begins Article VI, Administration.

nodes.title: 6.1 General.
nodes.summary: The Plan Administrator oversees Plan administration, with exclusive discretion to interpret the Plan, determine benefit eligibility and amounts, and resolve disputes. The Administrator may adopt or change operating rules and practices, appoint assistants, and create needed forms. Decisions are final and binding on affected parties, subject to Article VII’s claims procedure. For matters concerning the Administrator’s own Plan rights or benefits, the Committee performs these duties, and the Administrator cannot participate or vote.

nodes.title: 6.2 Allocation and Delegation of Duties.
nodes.summary: The Plan Administrator may delegate some or all Plan responsibilities by written instrument, authorize further delegation, and revoke delegations in the same manner. Delegates’ actions have the same effect as the Administrator’s, who is not liable for delegates’ acts or omissions. Delegates must periodically report on their duties. The text then introduces Article VII, Claims Procedure.

nodes.title: 7.1 General.
nodes.summary: Benefit claims must be filed in writing within one year after separation from service or all Plan-related benefit rights are forfeited. Claim denials must be issued within 60 days, or up to 120 days with special circumstances, and explain the reasons, Plan provisions, needed information, and review and ERISA rights. Claimants may appeal in writing within 60 days, inspect relevant documents, and submit comments; review decisions follow similar 60/120-day deadlines and disclosure requirements. Disability claims follow the cited DOL regulation. The text then begins Article VIII on miscellaneous provisions, including Plan amendment, suspension, or termination.

nodes.title: Claim Appeals and Disability Claims
nodes.summary: Claimants may appeal denials in writing to the Plan Administrator within 60 days, review relevant documents, and submit written comments. Review decisions are generally due within 60 days, or within 120 days if an extension is needed, and must explain the reasons and Plan provisions, access to relevant records, voluntary appeal options, and the right to sue under ERISA Section 502(a). Disability claims follow DOL Regulation 2560.503-1.

title: ARTICLE VIII. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

nodes.title: 8.1 Amendment, Suspension or Termination of Plan.
nodes.summary: The plan may be amended, suspended, or terminated, but not to forfeit existing participant accounts; following a qualifying change in control, it may be partially terminated and benefits distributed under specified Code Section 409A conditions. Benefits cannot generally be transferred or seized, except for qualifying domestic relations orders paid in a lump sum. Recipients must repay mistaken overpayments. The plan grants no employment, bonus, or award rights; bonuses are governed by their own plans. Employers or affiliates must withhold required employment taxes from compensation.

nodes.title: Plan Protections and Participant Rights
nodes.summary: The Plan may be amended, suspended, or terminated, but not to forfeit existing account balances; specified change-in-control termination and distributions must comply with Code Section 409A. Benefits cannot be assigned or seized, except for single-lump-sum distributions under qualifying domestic relations orders. Recipients must repay mistaken overpayments on request. The Plan provides no right to continued employment or to bonuses or awards, which are governed by their applicable plans or arrangements.

nodes.title: 8.6 Withholding and Employment Taxes.
nodes.summary: The Employer or a Related Affiliate withholds legally required employment taxes from current compensation and applicable federal, Puerto Rican, state, or local income taxes from Plan distributions. Participants or their beneficiaries are responsible for all income and excise taxes arising from Plan participation. The Plan binds and benefits Walmart, other Employers and their successors and assigns, and Participants and their beneficiaries, heirs, and legal representatives. Delaware law governs, except where preempted by federal law.

nodes.title: Tax Responsibilities and Successors
nodes.summary: Plan distributions are subject to required federal, Puerto Rican, state, and local income-tax withholding. The Participant or beneficiaries are responsible for all income and excise taxes arising from Plan participation. The Plan binds and benefits Walmart, other Employers and their successors and assigns, as well as the Participant, beneficiaries, heirs, and legal representatives.

title: WALMART INC. SUPPLEMENTAL EXECUTIVE RETIREMENT PLAN
summary: The text presents the table of contents and opening provisions of Walmart’s Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan, restated effective February 1, 2023. It explains the plan’s purpose, 409A compliance, unfunded status, and unsecured-creditor protections; defines key terms; and describes eligibility and participation, including limits on new entrants since February 1, 2013. The contents also outline provisions on accounts and credits, benefit payments, misconduct reductions, administration, claims and appeals, and miscellaneous matters such as amendments, taxes, and overpayment recovery.

title: ARTICLE IV PLAN ACCOUNTS AND CREDITS
summary: Accounts are bookkeeping measures only; funds remain Walmart’s property, and participants hold only an unsecured right to Plan benefits. Credits for the year ending January 31, 2012 cover specified missed or capped 401(k) profit-sharing contributions (calculated at 4%), plus discretionary Committee credits. For 2013, eligible bonus recipients receive a 4% credit on bonus amounts exceeding the compensation limit. No credits apply for years beginning February 1, 2013 or later, and initial credits require an aggregate minimum of $100. Accounts receive returns based on 401(k) investments or the default option for 2012, quarterly compounded interest through January 2023, and, from February 2023, participant-elected interest or deemed investment-option gains and losses. The Committee sets election windows and procedures; elections for gains and losses are irrevocable for the elected portion, default to interest, and do not require Walmart to invest funds.

title: ARTICLE V PAYMENT OF PLAN BENEFITS
summary: The Plan provides lump-sum cash benefits: retirement or disability payments go to the Participant within 90 days after the Pay Date; death benefits go to the Beneficiary within 90 days after the month of death; and other separations pay the Participant within 90 days after the Pay Date, subject to the vested percentage. For events on or before January 31, 2012, amounts use the applicable account value plus annual-compounded mid-term federal-rate interest; from February 1, 2012, amounts use account value through distribution. Participants may file or change primary and contingent beneficiary designations; absent a valid designation, the applicable 401(k) plan beneficiary controls. No benefits are payable before Separation from Service.

title: ARTICLE VI GROSS MISCONDUCT -- REDUCTION IN PLAN BENEFITS
summary: Gross misconduct during employment or any additional period in Walmart’s Statement of Ethics can reduce benefits: the Committee may recalculate the account without employer contributions and related gains or losses credited on or after January 31, 1996. Benefits and payments are contingent on compliance; participants or beneficiaries must repay any excess if misconduct is later found. The Committee administers and interprets the Plan, determines eligibility and benefits, adopts operating rules, may appoint assistance, and issues decisions binding subject to Article VIII claims procedures; members must recuse themselves from matters concerning their own benefits. The Committee may allocate duties to members or delegate them in writing, revoke those assignments, and require periodic reports; assigned actions carry Committee authority, and the Committee is not liable for assignees’ acts or omissions.

title: ARTICLE VIII CLAIMS AND APPEALS PROCEDURES
summary: Participants or beneficiaries must submit written benefit claims to the Committee within one year after separation from service; late claims eliminate any obligation to pay and further Plan rights. The Committee must notify claimants of denials within 60 days (45 for disability claims), with limited, timely-noticed extensions. Denial notices must state reasons, relevant Plan provisions, information needed to perfect the claim, and appeal procedures. Claimants may appeal in writing within 60 days (180 for disability claims), review relevant documents, and submit written comments. Review decisions are due within 60 days (45 for disability claims), extendable for special circumstances to 120 days (90 for disability claims), and must explain the reasons and cite Plan provisions.

nodes.title: ARTICLE I. GENERAL
nodes.summary: Walmart’s Officer Deferred Compensation Plan aims to attract and retain officers, reward their contributions, permit deferral of compensation and bonuses with credited earnings and incentive payments, and accept certain deferred 2005 Stock Incentive Plan awards. After prior amendments, including ending deferral elections effective February 1, 2012, and a 2018 renaming, Walmart restated the Plan effective February 1, 2023, to offer notional earnings tied to predetermined actual investments. The Plan dates to February 1, 1996, is generally administered in compliance with Code Section 409A, and preserves pre-2005 vested deferrals under Appendix A, which may not be materially modified except as expressly permitted. It is an unfunded ERISA plan for select management or highly compensated employees; payments come from Walmart’s general assets, participants have no claim to specific assets or trust or fiduciary rights, and payment rights are those of unsecured general creditors.

nodes.title: ARTICLE II. DEFINITIONS
nodes.summary: Defines the Plan’s terms, including accounts and credited deferrals, compensation, bonuses, equity and employer contributions; governing entities, committees, laws and plan years; participant and officer eligibility; misconduct, disability, retirement, separation from service, emergencies and related dates; investment and interest calculations; account types and distribution timing; and the meanings of stock awards, affiliates, prior agreements, and Walmart.

nodes.title: ARTICLE III. DEFERRED COMPENSATION/BONUSES AND EMPLOYER CONTRIBUTION CREDITS --ESTABLISHMENT OF ACCOUNTS
3.1 Deferred Compensation.
nodes.summary: Eligible Officers may elect to defer all or part of annual compensation, withheld proportionally across payroll periods, using approved forms, subject to a prohibition applying from the first payroll period after February 1, 2012. Elections are due by December 31 before the Plan Year, or within 30 days of first eligibility for newly eligible participants, with specified 24-month and prior-payment exceptions; such elections apply only to later payroll periods after receipt. For Plan Years beginning April 1, 2009, officers must allocate deferrals to Retirement Accounts and, for a first allocation, choose a distribution form. From February 1, 2010, they may also allocate to Scheduled In-Service Accounts and must designate each new account’s Scheduled Pay Date.

nodes.title: 3.2 Deferred Bonuses.
nodes.summary: Eligible Officers may defer all or part of MIP bonuses using approved forms, but not for performance periods beginning on or after February 1, 2012. Elections for periods beginning before 2009 follow prior Plan deadlines; from 2009 onward, they are due by the preceding December 31, or within 30 days of first eligibility for newly eligible participants, subject to specified prior-participation exceptions. Newly eligible elections apply only to post-election services, with the eligible bonus portion prorated by remaining calendar days. From 2009, officers must allocate deferrals to Retirement Accounts and choose a distribution form for a first allocation; from 2010, they may also use Scheduled In-Service Accounts and must designate a Scheduled Pay Date for a new account.

nodes.title: 3.3 Deferred Special Bonuses.
nodes.summary: Eligible Officers may defer all or part of Special Bonuses paid by Walmart or a designated participating affiliate using approved forms submitted to Executive Compensation; the election date is when the executed form is received. No elections may be made on or after February 1, 2012. Elections are generally due by the start of eligible employment, but prior or current participation in this or a 409A-aggregated plan bars elections unless the officer was ineligible for all such plans during the preceding 24 months or had received all prior amounts and was ineligible for subsequent participation by the final payment date. For elections from January 1, 2009, officers must also allocate deferrals to one or both Retirement Accounts and choose a distribution form for a first allocation. From February 1, 2010, they may also allocate to Scheduled In-Service Accounts and must designate a Scheduled Pay Date for a new account.

nodes.title: 3.4 Deferred Retention Bonuses.
nodes.summary: Eligible Officers may defer all or part of Retention Bonuses from Walmart or a Committee-designated participating affiliate by submitting an approved (including electronic) election to Executive Compensation. The election date is when the executed form is received; elections must be filed within 30 days after the officer obtains a legally binding right to the bonus, and none may be made on or after February 1, 2012. For elections from January 1, 2009, officers must allocate deferrals to one or both Retirement Accounts and, for a first allocation, choose a distribution form. From January 1, 2010, they may also allocate to Scheduled In-Service Accounts and must designate a Scheduled Pay Date for any new account.

nodes.title: 3.5 Incentive Payments.
nodes.summary: An Eligible Officer who becomes a Participant after December 31, 2008 must elect how to allocate Incentive Payments between Retirement Accounts within the earliest applicable initial-deferral election deadline under Sections 3.1–3.4. If no timely election is made, all payments are allocated to Retirement Account #1. The election, whether made or deemed, is irrevocable.

nodes.title: 3.6 Irrevocability of Deferral Elections.
nodes.summary: Deferral elections generally become irrevocable after their applicable deadlines, do not carry over to later years, and default allocations follow the prior year’s allocation or are split equally among Retirement Accounts. The text explains how elections end, continue, or resume after separation, rehire, loss of eligible status, or unpaid leave. Elections may be suspended after hardship distributions or for an approved unforeseeable emergency. Walmart may make discretionary, variably allocated Company Account credits, subject to Committee-set vesting and distribution only when vested. Deferred compensation is credited when it would otherwise have been paid in cash.

nodes.title: Deferral Suspensions and Employer Credits
nodes.summary: The page explains how deferral elections operate during unpaid leave: Section 3.1 elections resume upon return in the same Plan Year and remain effective for compensation paid during leave, while Sections 3.2–3.4 elections are unaffected. Elections are cancelled for six months after qualifying hardship distributions, or as determined by the Committee when stopping deferrals may relieve an unforeseeable emergency. Walmart may make discretionary Company Account credits, which vest under the Committee’s schedule and are distributed only to the vested extent.

nodes.title: 3.9 Crediting of Deferrals and Employer Contribution Credits.
nodes.summary: Sections 3.9–3.11 specify when deferred compensation, bonuses, equity, employer contribution credits, and incentive payments are credited; accounts are maintained until benefits are paid. Accounts are only measurement devices, remain Walmart’s property, and represent an unsecured promise to pay. Accounts are valued daily from April 1, 2008. Section 4.1 provides that, for Plan Years beginning February 1, 2023, participants receive a daily valuation-date credit, including monthly-compounded interest based on the prior valuation date’s account value, as elected under the plan.

nodes.title: Account Credits, Nature, and Valuation
nodes.summary: Deferred bonuses are credited when they would have been paid in cash; deferred equity when restrictions lapse or performance-share payment is processed; employer credits on the Committee’s specified date; and incentive payments on the specified Plan Year date. Accounts are maintained until benefits are fully paid. They are only measuring devices, not participant property or trust funds; all amounts remain Walmart’s property, and benefits are an unsecured promise. Effective April 1, 2008, accounts are valued daily on each Valuation Date.

The section governs elections to defer compensation, MIP, Special and Retention Bonuses, including eligibility, deadlines, prior-participation exceptions, allocation among Retirement or Scheduled In-Service Accounts, distribution-form and pay-date choices, and limits on deferrals. It sets allocation defaults and irrevocability rules, explains how elections operate or end after leave, separation, rehire, status changes, hardship distributions, or emergencies, and permits discretionary employer credits subject to vesting. It also specifies crediting dates for deferrals, bonuses, equity, employer credits and incentive payments; account maintenance, daily valuation and interest credits; and clarifies that accounts are measurement devices, Walmart property, and an unsecured promise to pay.

nodes.title: ARTICLE IV. ADDITIONS TO ACCOUNTS -- CREDITED EARNINGS AND INCENTIVE PAYMENTS
nodes.summary: Beginning with Plan Years on or after February 1, 2023, Participants may elect account interest compounded monthly or deemed investment-option gains and losses; absent an election, interest applies, and investment elections are irrevocable for the elected portion. Walmart need not actually invest funds. Incentive payments apply to eligible deferred compensation, bonuses, and earnings, excluding scheduled in-service amounts, amounts above 20% of annual base compensation, specified bonus/equity categories, and employer credits. Continuous employment earns 20% incentives after 10 years and annually thereafter, then 10% incentives after 15 years and annually thereafter, under specified lookback rules. Partial incentives may apply upon death, disability, or qualifying separation after 20 years’ service or age 55, subject to five years’ participation; payment timing and associated interest are specified. A legacy rule protects qualifying separations near Plan Year-end for Plan Years beginning before March 31, 2009.

nodes.title: ARTICLE V. PAYMENT OF PLAN BENEFITS
Lump Sum Distributions.
nodes.summary: Scheduled in-service accounts are paid as a lump sums within 90 days after their scheduled pay date, valued on that date; an earlier separation or death-triggered distribution instead follows Sections 5.2 or 5.3. Separation other than retirement or death results in a lump-sum account distribution. On retirement, scheduled in-service accounts are paid in a lump sum, while Company and Retirement Accounts follow the participant’s effective election among the forms provided. Section 5.2 lump sums are paid within 90 days after the Separation Pay Date and valued as of the preceding month’s last day.

nodes.title: Installment Distributions.
nodes.summary: Annual installments begin within 90 days after the first January 31 following separation from service, unless that date precedes the Separation Pay Date, in which case they begin within 90 days after that date; later installments begin within 90 days after each successive January 31 until paid in full. Interest-crediting account portions are paid in equal installments amortizing their lump-sum value over the installment period at the applicable Plan Year interest rate. Portions credited with earnings, gains, and losses are paid in substantially equal installments based on the remaining balance divided by remaining payments. If a participant dies before separation or benefit commencement, the account is distributed under an elected form specified in Section 5.3(b) or (c), subject to Section 5.4. Only one payment form may be elected for all beneficiary levels; absent an effective election, a lump sum under Section 5.3(b) applies.

nodes.title: Installment Distributions.
nodes.summary: Annual installments begin within 90 days after the first January 31 on or after a participant’s death and continue annually until paid in full. Interest-bearing account portions are amortized in equal installments at the applicable Plan Year rate; portions credited with investment gains and losses are divided using the remaining balance and payments. If a participant dies after installments start, payments generally continue to beneficiaries, except a lump-sum election requires remaining installments to be paid as a lump sum within 90 days after the death month. Participants may designate or change primary and contingent beneficiaries for both accounts together; default beneficiaries are spouse, children, parents, siblings, then estate. If a beneficiary dies before full payment, benefits pass to remaining beneficiaries at that level, then the next level or the deceased beneficiary’s default beneficiaries. On retirement or death, distributions may be a lump sum, installments over up to 15 years, or—only on death—a combination. Installments require an account value of at least $50,000; otherwise payment defaults to a lump sum.

nodes.title: Retirement Accounts.
nodes.summary: The text sets rules for allocating 2008 participant balances and later deferrals or incentive payments among Retirement Accounts based on payment elections, including transition relief and irrevocability provisions. Company Accounts default to lump-sum payment. Subsequent elections must meet timing, delay, completion, and filing limits; invalid elections are disregarded in favor of the latest valid one. It also permits discretionary emergency distributions, limited to demonstrated need and subject to funding order and possible tax-deduction delays. Gross misconduct forfeits employer credits and incentive payments, reduces credited gains and remaining installments, but never forfeits participant deferrals; excess payments must be repaid.

The section governs benefit payment timing, valuation, and forms after separation, retirement, or death. Benefits may be paid as lump sums or annual installments, with distinct rules for account types, interest or investment earnings, election deadlines, and default forms. It covers beneficiary designations, succession, and payments when a participant or beneficiary dies, including installment limits and minimum account thresholds. It also addresses Retirement Account allocations, election rules, emergency distributions, forfeiture for gross misconduct, and repayment of excess benefits.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VI. ADMINISTRATION
nodes.summary: The Committee administers the Plan, interprets its terms, determines eligibility and benefits, resolves disputes, adopts administrative rules, and may appoint assistance. Its decisions are binding, subject to claims procedures; members cannot decide matters concerning their own benefits. The Committee may assign or delegate responsibilities in writing, revoke those arrangements, and require periodic reports; actions taken have Committee authority, and the Committee is not liable for assignees’ or delegates’ acts or omissions. Benefit claims must be filed in writing within one year of separation from service. Denials require timely written notice stating reasons, Plan provisions, needed information, and appeal procedures. Claimants may appeal within 60 days, inspect relevant documents, and submit written comments. Review decisions are due within 60 days, or up to 120 days in special circumstances, and must explain the decision and cite relevant Plan provisions.

nodes.title: ARTICLE VIII. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
nodes.summary: The plan may be amended, suspended, or terminated, but generally cannot distribute accounts before separation from service or forfeit existing balances; a change-in-control partial termination may permit distributions if related aggregated plans are also terminated and liquidated. Benefits cannot be assigned or seized, except for qualifying domestic relations orders paid in a lump sum. Mistaken payments must be repaid. The plan grants no employment, bonus, or stock-award rights; required employment and distribution tax withholding applies, while participants or beneficiaries bear resulting income and excise taxes. The plan binds the parties and their successors, and Delaware law governs unless federally preempted.

summary: Appendix A presents Walmart Inc.’s Officer Deferred Compensation Plan, an unfunded, generally Section 409A-compliant ERISA plan preserving certain pre-2005 vested deferrals. It covers the Plan’s purpose, history, definitions, eligibility, deferral elections, account credits and valuation, investment-linked earnings and incentive payments, benefit forms and timing, beneficiaries, emergencies, forfeitures and repayments. It also sets out Committee administration and claims and appeals procedures, plus amendment and termination limits, assignment protections, tax withholding, employment-rights disclaimers, successor obligations, and governing law.

title: APPENDIX A
key_items: WALMART INC. OFFICER DEFERRED COMPENSATION PLAN
summary: Appendix A governs deferred amounts vested by December 31, 2004 and restricts material changes under Code Section 409A. It presents Walmart’s Officer Deferred Compensation Plan: its goals, history and effective dates; its unfunded, unsecured-creditor status and payment sources; and definitions covering the Code, Committee, deferred compensation and bonuses, disability, early retirement, eligibility, fiscal and plan years, grandfathered accounts, gross misconduct, incentive payments, participants, affiliates, retirement, termination, unforeseeable emergencies, and annual valuation dates. The disability note specifies Social Security-based criteria and limits later changes.

title: ARTICLE III. DEFERRED COMPENSATION AND BONUSES--ESTABLISHMENT OF ACCOUNTS
summary: The article sets rules for officers’ salary and bonus deferrals: election forms and deadlines, irrevocability, cessation or continuation after appointment, loss of officer status, leave, or termination, prorating bonuses, and the need for new elections each year. Deferred compensation, bonuses, and incentive payments are credited to Committee-maintained bookkeeping accounts on specified dates. These accounts only measure benefits, remain Walmart’s property, and represent an unsecured payment promise. Accounts are valued annually, reflecting credits, interest, and emergency distributions. Amendments provide daily interest from 2008, revised Plan Year timing from 2009, and, for Plan Years from 2023, an irrevocable choice between interest and deemed investment-option returns, with default interest, Committee-set election procedures, no required actual investment, and special valuation rules for lump sums and installments; the amendments are stated not to be material modifications under Code Section 409A.

title: ARTICLE IV. ADDITIONS TO ACCOUNTS -- CREDITED EARNINGS AND INCENTIVE PAYMENTS
summary: Article IV sets rules for credited earnings and incentive payments to Grandfathered Accounts. Annual earnings use a Committee-set rate, generally calculated on prior account value, half of current-year deferrals, and qualifying deferred bonuses; emergency distributions require month-based prorating. A note fixes the rate formula at the 10-year Treasury rate plus 270 basis points, with no 2005 adjustment. Incentives preserve prior awards, avoid duplication, and generally apply to recognized deferrals and earnings, excluding amounts above 20% of base compensation. Continuous employment earns 20% awards after ten years and annually thereafter, then 10% awards after fifteen years and annually thereafter, subject to specified lookback periods and exclusions. Prorated next awards may apply upon retirement, early retirement, death, or disability after five years; qualifying terminations between fiscal- and plan-year ends preserve otherwise-earned awards. Award timing depends on lump-sum or installment distributions. Appendix A incentives are frozen; from 2005, awards are made under the Plan.

title: ARTICLE V. PAYMENT OF PLAN BENEFITS

nodes.title: Plan Benefit Payment and Termination Rules
key_items: (b) Termination on Last Business Day of Plan Year.
nodes.summary: Benefits generally cannot be paid before retirement, early retirement, termination, disability, or death, except for an unforeseeable emergency. For termination for other reasons, benefits are paid as a lump sum within 60 days after the termination month ends. Participants age 50 or older may instead elect substantially equal annual installments for up to 15 years, subject to account-value restrictions. If termination occurs on the Plan Year’s last business day, the lump sum is the Grandfathered Account value at the applicable Annual Valuation Date plus prorated interest through payment.

nodes.title: (c) Termination on Other Than Last Business Day of Plan Year.
nodes.summary: For termination on a date other than the Plan Year’s last weekday, the lump sum includes the Grandfathered Account value at the preceding Annual Valuation Date, plus prorated interest on that value through distribution; Deferred Compensation for the termination year, plus prorated interest on half that amount over the same period; and any Incentive Payments provided under Section 4.2(f). Interest rates are determined under Section 4.1.

nodes.title: (d) Death.
nodes.summary: If a Participant dies before receiving full Plan benefits under Section 5.2, payments are made or continued to the Section 5.5 beneficiary according to the Participant’s Section 5.6 death-benefit election. For Participants in pay status who die on or after October 1, 2003, if no designated beneficiary exists or survives, benefits are paid as a lump sum to the estate.

nodes.title: (e) Installment Distributions.
nodes.summary: For annual installment distributions, the Grandfathered Account is generally valued on the January 31 coinciding with or following termination, using the prior annual valuation, prorated interest, termination-year deferred compensation, eligible incentive payments, and specified prorated interest on deferred compensation. If termination occurs on a weekday January 31, the calculation instead uses the next annual valuation, prorated interest through the following January 31, and eligible incentive payments. Benefits are paid in equal annual installments that amortize the calculated amount over the installment period, with interest at the termination-year Plan rate. Payments begin January 31 following termination and continue annually until fully distributed; for January 31 terminations, the first payment is the next January 31.

nodes.title: 5.3 Retirement, Early Retirement, and Disability Benefits.
nodes.summary: Upon termination due to retirement, early retirement, or disability, a participant’s benefits are paid as a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over no more than 15 years, subject to Section 5.6’s minimum account value restrictions and the participant’s distribution election under that section.

nodes.title: (b) Lump Sum Distributions.
nodes.summary: Lump-sum benefits are paid within 60 days after the end of the month in which retirement, early retirement, or disability occurs. The amount depends on whether the event falls on the Plan Year’s last business day. On that day, it includes the Grandfathered Account value at the coincident or next Annual Valuation Date, prorated interest through payment at the rate for the distribution year, and any applicable Incentive Payment. On other dates, it includes the account value at the prior Annual Valuation Date plus prorated interest at the Section 4.1 rate, current-year Deferred Compensation, applicable Incentive Payments, and prorated interest on 50% of that Deferred Compensation.

nodes.title: (c) Installment Distributions.
nodes.summary: For annual installments, the Grandfathered Account is valued as of the January 31 on or after retirement, early retirement, or disability, including the prior valuation-date balance, prorated interest, current-year deferred compensation and eligible incentive payments, plus specified prorated interest on deferred compensation. If the event occurs on a non-weekend January 31, valuation instead uses the next Annual Valuation Date, prorated interest through the following January 31, and eligible incentive payments. Benefits are paid in equal annual amounts that amortize the value over the installment period at the applicable Plan Year interest rate, beginning January 31 after the event (or the next January 31 if the event occurred on January 31). If the participant dies before full payment, benefits go to the designated beneficiary under the separate death-benefit election; for pay-status participants dying on or after October 1, 2003, absent a surviving designated beneficiary, payment is a lump sum to the estate.

nodes.title: 5.4 Death Benefits.
nodes.summary: Upon a participant’s death, benefits go to the designated beneficiary as a lump sum or, subject to Section 5.6’s minimum-account restrictions, substantially equal annual installments over no more than 15 years, according to the applicable distribution election. A lump sum is paid within 60 days after the month of death. Its calculation uses the Grandfathered Account value on the valuation date specified according to whether death occurred on the Plan Year’s last business day, prorated interest through payment, and any applicable Incentive Payment. Installments are based on the account value as of January 31 coinciding with or following death, calculated under Section 5.3(c), and amortized equally with interest at the rate for the year of death. The first installment is paid on that January 31 and then each January 31 until fully paid; if death occurs on January 31, the first payment is the following January 31.

nodes.title: 5.5 Designation of Beneficiary.
nodes.summary: Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries, and payment proportions, by submitting the Committee-prescribed written or electronic form. One designation applies to both the Account and any Grandfathered Account; different beneficiaries cannot be named for each. Designations may be changed, and the latest written designation on file before death controls. If no beneficiary is designated or the beneficiary predeceases the Participant, benefits go to the estate. A properly filed designation under a Prior Agreement remains effective until modified under this section.

nodes.title: 5.6 Form of Distribution.
nodes.summary: Eligible participants whose employment ends due to retirement, early retirement disability or death, or after age 50, may elect a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments for up to 15 years. For terminations on or after October 1, 2003, installments are available only when the Grandfathered Account exceeds $50,000 at lump-sum valuation; otherwise payment defaults to a lump sum. Elections filed on Committee forms generally cover total Plan benefits, though death benefits under Sections 5.2–5.4 may have separate elections. Elections for Sections 5.2 or 5.3 benefits must generally be filed at least six months before the qualifying event; otherwise the latest timely election applies. This waiting period does not apply to death benefits. Prior Agreement elections remain effective until amended, but Section 5.4 death benefits default to a lump sum absent an affirmative contrary election. Participants with under six months’ Plan participation may use their initial election. For qualifying terminations on or after June 1, 1999, after age 50, a Section 5.3 installment election applies automatically without participant consent or ratification.

nodes.title: 5.7 Reductions Arising from a Participant’s Gross Misconduct.
nodes.summary: A participant’s benefits depend on avoiding Gross Misconduct during employment with Walmart, its affiliates or entities in which it has an ownership interest, and any additional period specified by Walmart’s ethics rules. If the Committee finds misconduct, all Incentive Payments and related credited earnings are forfeited; earnings on Grandfathered Account amounts derived from Deferred Compensation or Deferred Bonuses are recalculated at half the applicable positive rate. Net losses are unchanged, and Deferred Compensation and Deferred Bonuses themselves cannot be forfeited. If misconduct is discovered after payment, the participant or beneficiary must repay any excess received to Walmart or the applicable affiliate.

nodes.title: 5.8 Distributions for Unforeseeable Emergencies.
nodes.summary: Upon a participant’s written application, the Committee may, at its sole discretion, authorize an immediate distribution of all or part of plan benefits for an unforeseeable emergency, limited to what is reasonably needed. If the participant also terminates employment during the same fiscal year as the distribution, and termination occurs on a date other than the fiscal year’s last business day (excluding weekends), the lump sum under Sections 5.2, 5.3, or 5.4 is reduced by the emergency distribution; the interest equivalent is calculated consistently with Section 4.1.

summary: The Article governs when and how Plan benefits are paid for termination, retirement, early retirement, disability, and death, including lump-sum and installment calculations, valuation dates, interest, payment deadlines, and installment schedules. It addresses beneficiary designations and distribution elections, eligibility and account-value limits, death payments to estates, and the effect of gross misconduct, including forfeitures, recalculations, and repayment. It also permits discretionary emergency distributions and explains their effect on later termination benefits.

title: ARTICLE VI. ADMINISTRATION
summary: The Committee administers the Plan, with exclusive authority to interpret its terms, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and resolve disputes over participant or beneficiary rights. It may establish, change, or repeal administrative rules and appoint others to assist with administration and forms. Its decisions are final and binding on Walmart, affiliates, participants, beneficiaries, and others affected, subject to Article VII’s claims process. A Committee member must not participate or vote on matters concerning their own Plan rights or benefits.

title: ARTICLE VII. CLAIMS PROCEDURE
summary: Claims must be filed in writing with the Committee or its delegate. Denials must be communicated within 60 days, with written reasons, relevant Plan provisions, information needed to perfect the claim, and review procedures. Claimants or authorized representatives may appeal in writing within 60 days, review pertinent documents, and submit written comments. The Committee must decide appeals within 60 days, or within 120 days if special circumstances require an extension, and provide a written decision stating reasons and applicable Plan provisions.

title: ARTICLE VIII. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
summary: Walmart may amend, suspend, or terminate the Plan, but cannot eliminate participants’ existing Grandfathered Accounts. Benefits cannot generally be assigned, pledged, borrowed against, or otherwise alienated, except for a qualifying domestic relations order paid in a lump sum. The Plan grants no employment or bonus rights. Walmart or affiliates will withhold legally required taxes; participants, beneficiaries, or estates are responsible for resulting income and excise taxes. Recipients must repay mistaken or excess payments upon request. The Plan binds and benefits the participating employers and their successors, participants, and their beneficiaries, heirs, and representatives, and is governed by Delaware law unless federal law preempts it.

nodes.summary: A list of pending non-MDL federal court cases as of March 3, 2023, providing case names, defendants, federal district courts, and filing dates. Most are Puerto Rico municipalities’ cases against Teva Pharmaceuticals, filed in November 2022; others involve Alabama and Oklahoma counties, cities, a physician, and a minor plaintiff suing pharmaceutical companies, pharmacies, distributors, or Walmart, across several federal districts, from April to November 2022.

summary: Walmart CEO C. Douglas McMillon and CFO John David Rainey certify that the company’s 2023 Form 10-K complies with applicable Securities Exchange Act requirements and fairly presents its financial condition and results; both certifications are dated March 17, 2023. The section also lists opioid-related pending state-court cases and their parties, courts, and filing dates; four scheduled state-court trials; and pending non-MDL federal cases, with parties, courts, and filing dates, all as of March 3, 2023.
